quotes.story_title: Ask HN: How do you handle marketing as a solo technical founder?

quotes.text:
> This makes it seem like your claims exist solely for marketing, boosting Google SEO rankings, or getting crawled by AI models like ChatGPT.

Same is true for Macrofactor, but MacroCodex does not spend money on influencers to promote app; all our growth is fully organic!

Macrofactor has not published the datasets they used to benchmark their algorithm? https://macrofactor.com/algorithm-accuracy/

Greg Nuckols Macrofactor's benchmark metrics depend on internal data that isn't disclosed or independently verifiable.

So the published accuracy claims don't tell us much. It's like a student saying, “I scored 99% on a test,” but not showing anyone the test questions or their answers. You have no way to independently verify whether the score actually reflects how well they perform.

The number might be completely accurate, but without seeing the benchmark dataset, there's no way for anyone outside the company to reproduce or properly evaluate the claim.

>I am currently a MacroFactor user

We already beat Macrofactor in both maintenance calorie accuracy and the speed of maintenance calorie updates.

Macrofactor costs $72 a year while Macrocodex is free. 
Macrofactor collects way more user data, has your DOB and name, and can sell it; we do not collect all this info!

>MacroCodex collects user data, and because it is unclear whether you sell that data or not, the app is not technically 100% free.

How can we even sell data we do not collect?
